clearedSpotChecks.check: A pool whose currency is the T14 configurable account precompile address 0xAACC... (or any address that gains a precompile at a fork): can it hold or release value before or after T14?
clearedSpotChecks.note: eth_getCode for 0xAACC000000000000000000000000000000000000 on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz (tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748, block 0x3091650) returns 0x, and eth_call of balanceOf(PoolManager) from the PoolManager returns success with empty data. The source is compiled with solc 0.8.26 (foundry.toml:6, src/PoolManager.sol:2), whose high level call with a uint256 return reverts when the return data is shorter than 32 bytes, so sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288) via balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96) reverts. Without sync, _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364) credits only msg.value to address(0) and never this currency, so no account can hold positive delta, liquidity or ERC-6909 claims in it; take (src/PoolManager.sol:290-296) only debits the caller. The recorded T14 simulation (t14probe.log) shows every call reverting after T14, which keeps the same result. Agreed.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-1078 for Tempo: does tempo v1.19.1 commit a speculative prewarm result without re-running the transaction, in block validation or block building, so that settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364) could measure a balance rise on stale state?
clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched reth 167933d crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_processor/mod.rs: prewarm_results is built only when self.reuse_prewarm_results, PrewarmMode::Transactions, no decoded BAL, cfg_reuses_prewarm_results and self.evm_config.reuses_prewarm_results() all hold. reth crates/evm/evm/src/lib.rs lines 684-686 give the trait default false. Tempo a9d6748 crates/evm/src/lib.rs has impl ConfigureEvm for TempoEvmConfig at line 224 and contains no reuses_prewarm_results override (grep on the fetched file finds none). Validation therefore re-executes every transaction whatever the tree flag. The builder replay path was not re-read by me; a builder that commits a wrong result is operator level and its block fails other validators' execution check. Agreed.

clearedSpotChecks.check: 21,537 new MULMOD, ADDMOD and FullMath high-half vectors (maxmod.py, maxmod2.py) aimed at ruint 1.21.1's end-around carry path and the 1.21.0 fault condition.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Downloaded https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.21.1.crate; sha256 a0de3fa9b4dac39cc2bd65679bacf9f531899d933605e2963b40c2129cdb55f2 matches the cited checksum. knuth.rs lines 131-136 skip the top quotient limb only when the top numerator limb is 0 and the next two limbs are strictly below the divisor's top two, and modular.rs lines 118-127 reduce modulo 2^256-1 by end-around carry with 2^256-1 mapped to 0; both are exact. I ran 124 independent MULMOD vectors (random 256 bit operands with modulus 2^256-1, moduli built from the product's high half, and the edges (M,M,M), (2^128,2^128,M), (M,1,M), (2^255,2,M)) as create-call eth_call on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz and https://arc.drpc.org: 0 mismatches on both. The mulmod(a, b, not(0)) step of FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24) therefore gets the exact high half on both networks. Agreed.
